title: Club Membership: how the recurring dues discount is chosen and applied
content:
## Scope
This document states how Club Membership chooses between its two candidate discount percentages for a recurring dues charge, and how the chosen percentage combines with the tier's own original monthly dues amount to produce the billed amount.

## Rule
The two candidate discount percentages are evaluated independently of one another; the discount percentage actually applied to a recurring dues charge is the higher of the two candidates, never the two candidates combined together. The chosen percentage is applied once, directly to the member's tier own original monthly dues amount; it is never applied to any amount that has already been discounted. Because a recurring dues charge bills one monthly cycle at a time rather than a lump-sum prepayment, the tier's own multi-month prepay discount percentage never enters this comparison for a recurring dues charge. The billed amount is the original monthly dues amount multiplied by one minus the chosen percentage, rounded to 2 decimal places only at the end of the calculation, with no intermediate rounding.

## Worked example (hypothetical)
Suppose a member's tier own original monthly dues amount is $100.00, the member's linked employer partnership candidate percentage is 10 percent, and the member's own tier student discount candidate percentage is 15 percent. The two candidates are not added together to reach 25 percent; the higher of the two, 15 percent, is the one applied. The billed amount is $100.00 reduced by 15 percent of itself, giving $85.00.

## Points of judgement
A member whose linked employer partnership candidate is higher than their own tier's student discount candidate has the employer-linked candidate applied instead, never both together; a member with a nonzero multi-month prepay discount percentage on their tier still has that prepay percentage excluded from this particular comparison, since it does not apply to a recurring dues charge at all under this basis.
